claim: The bromide-substituted electrolyte conducted lithium ions almost twice as well as the chloride-only reference at room temperature.
evidence: BrAG-6 pellets reached an ionic conductivity of 7.4 mS/cm at 25 degrees C, nearly double the 3.9 mS/cm of CLAG-0. The activation energy fell from 0.29 eV for CLAG-0 to 0.23 eV for BrAG-6, consistent with a softer anion framework.
label: supported

claim: Glass-glass packaged perovskite cells began to degrade from their edges, whereas cells with the trilayer barrier degraded evenly.
evidence: Under damp heat, FAST cells reached T80 after a median of 1,740 hours, against 960 hours for GG-butyl cells and 41 hours for unencapsulated cells. Failure in GG-butyl cells started at the edges, where lead iodide formation was visible after 700 hours, whereas FAST cells degraded uniformly.
label: supported

claim: Just under a third of the hot tank's standby heat loss escaped through its foundation.
evidence: The foundation accounted for 31 percent of hot-tank loss, the walls for 52 percent and the roof for 17 percent. Installing the ARC-40 ring in month 9 reduced foundation loss by 0.4 kW.
label: supported

claim: NFM-felt lost only 0.8 percent of its iron over 2,000 hours at constant current because molybdate anchors the iron sites.
evidence: Under constant current at 500 mA/cm^2, NFM-felt cells degraded by only 11 microvolts per hour over 2,000 hours, a total voltage rise of 22 mV, and inductively coupled plasma analysis showed an iron loss of 0.8 percent of the initial inventory.
label: partially_supported

claim: FAST cells kept 91.4 percent of their efficiency after 1,000 hours of one-sun tracking at 65 degrees C, outperforming glass-butyl packaged cells in the same test.
evidence: Lead iodide was detected in unencapsulated films from the 0 degrees C step onward. Under one-sun tracking at 65 degrees C, FAST cells retained 91.4 percent of initial efficiency after 1,000 hours.
label: partially_supported

claim: BrAG-6 cells can be cycled against lithium metal anodes without forming dendrites.
evidence: Cells used a nickel-rich layered oxide cathode, designated NR-88, mixed with electrolyte in a 70 to 30 mass ratio at an areal capacity of 3.1 mAh/cm^2, a 520 micrometre electrolyte separator, and a lithium-indium alloy anode.
label: unsupported

claim: The TN-131 ternary salt is cheaper per tonne than binary sodium-potassium nitrate.
evidence: The salt chemistry remained stable. Nitrite content rose from 0.4 to 1.9 weight percent over 18 months, and carbonate stayed below 0.25 weight percent.
label: unsupported

claim: The FAST barrier can be deposited on flexible plastic substrates without cracking.
evidence: First, a 22 nm alumina layer was grown by thermal atomic layer deposition at 85 degrees C using trimethylaluminium and water. Second, a 1.8 micrometre fluorinated siloxane layer was spin coated from a solvent-free oligomer and cured under ultraviolet light at room temperature.
label: unsupported

claim: Under the IRLP-24 protocol, NFM-felt degraded faster than the molybdate-free NF-ref catalyst.
evidence: Over the full IRLP-24 test NFM-felt degraded at a mean rate of 38 microvolts per hour, more than three times its constant-current rate, while NF-ref degraded at 96 microvolts per hour and lost 4.6 percent of its iron.
label: contradicted

claim: The Corvane Ridge pilot achieved its highest monthly round-trip efficiency in January.
evidence: The best single month was July at 95.4 percent and the worst was January at 87.6 percent, when trace heating of pipes and the cold-tank drain line added up to 210 kWh per day.
label: contradicted
